adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb, the `members` action previously did `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`, which in Discourse controllers yields a top-level JSON array of serialized users. The diff changes it to `render json: { members: serialize_data(...), meta: { ... } }`, i.e., a JSON object with `members` and `meta` keys. There is no conditional fallback or alternate endpoint; callers of GET /groups/:group_id/members now receive a different top-level shape. The frontend code in this diff was updated accordingly (`result.members`, `result.meta`), confirming the intended shape change, but any other consumers expecting an array would break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — group.users.delete(user_id)` is called with a raw user id and no membership check; if `user_id` is not a current member this raises an unhandled `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`/type-mismatch that propagates as a 500 instead of a graceful JSON error

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `remove_member` does `user_id = params.require(:user_id).to_i` and then calls `group.users.delete(user_id)`. For ActiveRecord associations, `delete` on a `has_many`/`has_many :through` association accepts ids and issues a SQL delete on the join/association without raising if the id isn’t currently associated; it typically returns the number of records affected (often 0) rather than throwing `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`. Because the code uses `to_i`, there’s also no type-mismatch exception path here. So the claimed unhandled exception/500 on non-membership is not verifiable from this diff and is likely a misreading of how `association.delete` behaves.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — limit` param has no upper bound (defaults to 50 but a client can pass `limit=999999`), letting a request force full unpaginated materialization/serialization of a huge group again

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then runs `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` and serializes the resulting `members`. There is no upper bound/clamp on `limit`, so a client can pass an arbitrarily large `limit` value (e.g. 999999), causing the server to fetch and serialize a very large number of users in one request, which is a real performance/DoS risk introduced/preserved by this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:23 — offset` param is taken directly from user input with no upper bound; a large offset against a huge automatic group (e.g. trust_level_0 with hundreds of thousands of rows) forces Postgres to scan and discard that many rows via `OFFSET`, an easy DoS/expensive-query vector

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `GroupsController#members` now applies pagination to *all* groups and sets `offset = params[:offset].to_i` with no clamping or maximum. It then executes `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. A client can supply an arbitrarily large `offset`, which will generate an `OFFSET n` query; in Postgres large OFFSET values typically require scanning/skipping many rows, making it an expensive-query/DoS vector against large groups. There is no upper bound or `min(offset, total)` here (contrast with the JS model which clamps offset client-side, but server-side remains unbounded).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:38 — removeMember`'s `.then()` calls `self.findMembers()` but does not `return` it, so if the member-list reload fails after a successful delete, that rejection is swallowed and the outer promise resolves as if everything succeeded

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Discourse.Group#removeMember` returns `Discourse.ajax(...).then(function() { self.findMembers(); });`. Because the `.then` callback does not `return self.findMembers()`, the promise returned by `removeMember` resolves after the DELETE succeeds, regardless of whether the subsequent `findMembers()` request fails. Any rejection from `findMembers()` is not chained to (and therefore not propagated by) the outer promise, which can cause callers/UI to treat the overall operation as successful while the refresh silently fails. This is a concrete, verifiable promise-chaining defect introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:49 — addMembers`'s `.then()` calls `self.findMembers()` without returning it, so a failed reload after a successful add is silently dropped instead of propagating to callers

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, `addMembers` returns `Discourse.ajax(...).then(function() { self.findMembers(); })` but does not `return self.findMembers()` from inside the `then`. Since `findMembers()` itself performs an async `Discourse.ajax(...)` and returns its promise, failing to return it means the `addMembers()` promise resolves as soon as the `then` callback finishes (with `undefined`), without waiting for the reload and without propagating reload failures to callers. This is a concrete behavioral bug in the diff (same pattern also exists in `removeMember`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — group.users.delete(user_id)` removes the membership row directly instead of going through the `Group#remove` method used elsewhere (mirrors `group.add(user)` at line 73), likely skipping side-effect cleanup (e.g. clearing `primary_group_id`, permission/trust recalculation) and leaving stale group-derived authorization state on the user

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, membership removal previously went through `group.remove(user)` (see the removed `update_patch` code where deletions call `group.remove(user)`). The new `remove_member` action instead calls `group.users.delete(user_id)`, bypassing the Group-level API that is used elsewhere and is the logical counterpart to `group.add(user)` used in `add_members`. Since `Group#remove` clearly exists and was intentionally used before, directly deleting via the association is a verifiable behavioral change that can skip any logic encapsulated in `Group#remove` (callbacks, cleanup, bookkeeping). adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — usernames.split(",")` iterates with no cap on the number of entries, so a single request can trigger an unbounded number of `User.find_by_username` lookups and `group.add` calls

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` method, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then `usernames.split(",").each do |username| ... User.find_by_username(username) ... group.add(user)`. There is no validation or cap on how many comma-separated usernames can be submitted, so (within HTTP/request-size limits) a single request can force an arbitrarily large number of database lookups and membership-add operations, creating a clear potential for excessive work/DoS. This behavior is directly present in the diff and not merely stylistic.
